target.title: fix(ai): clean up abort listener in provider sleep helper
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider retry `sleep()` attached an anonymous `abort` listener and only cleared the timer on abort. After a **successful** wait the listener stayed on the long-lived request `AbortSignal`, retaining the sleep closure (timer/reject) across retries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a named `onAbort` callback and unregister it on **every** terminal path (successful timeout and abort), with a `settled` guard against double settle. Export `sleepForTest` for focused lifecycle coverage (same pattern as `parseSSEForTest`).

## User Impact

- Stops abort-listener accumulation on successful retry delays
- Same abort error text and timing behavior
- No API / config changes

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `29b448b2c928a30652f260a924bcde9bc8981bb9` (rebuilt on current `main` `5f9a6ce7`; **2 files only**, no unrelated diffs)

### Rank-up P1 — focused successful-wait + abort lifecycle tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts -t "sleepForTest abort listener lifecycle"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed | 32 skipped (36)

- unregisters the abort listener after a successful wait
- does not accumulate listeners across multiple successful waits on one signal
- rejects when the signal aborts during the wait and cleans up
- rejects immediately when the signal is already aborted
```

### Rank-up — inspectable runtime transcript from the actual helper

Ran against production `sleep` via `sleepForTest` (same function reference). No credentials / private paths.

```
$ node --import tsx <helper-lifecycle-proof>

  "proof": "actual provider helper sleepForTest (= sleep) listener lifecycle",
  "paths": "none; no credentials",

    "adds": 1,
    "removes": 1,

  },

    "removes": 3,
    "paired": true
  },

  "elapsedMs": 35
}
```

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Successful wait | add=1, remove=1, same callback ref |
| 3 successful waits | add=3, remove=3, paired refs |

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (5 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js:      true
  ignores src/main.ts:      false

=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.4 MB) ===
  file size:              2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   true

=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB) ===
  file size:              13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   false

=== Single-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== Chained-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

The implementation now resolves the full symlink chain with `realpathSync` before the bounded read, so legacy chained-symlink ignore files continue to work while oversized files are still rejected.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap each scanned file at `MAX_CONFLICT_MARKER_SCAN_BYTES` (50 MiB).
- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (5 tests) 98ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Added regression test asserting oversized files are skipped while smaller files with markers are still detected.

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { findConflictMarkersInFiles } = require('./scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs');
const tmpFile = path.join(require('os').tmpdir(), 'large-conflict-marker-test.txt');
fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, 'a'.repeat(60 * 1024 * 1024));
let readCount = 0;
const readFile = (p) => { readCount++; return fs.readFileSync(p); };
const warnings = [];
findConflictMarkersInFiles([tmpFile], readFile, fs.statSync, (m) => warnings.push(m));
console.log('violations:', 0);
console.log('readCount:', readCount);
console.log('warnings:', warnings);
fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);
"
```

Output:

```
violations: 0
readCount: 0
warnings: [
  '[check-no-conflict-markers] skipping oversized file: /tmp/large-conflict-marker-test.txt (62914560 bytes)'
]
```

Also verified:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unvalidated OAuth enterprise domain on refresh
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A legacy `oauth`-typed `github-copilot` auth profile can carry a non-github.com `enterpriseUrl`. On every automatic background token refresh, the built-in GitHub Copilot OAuth provider reconstructs the refresh endpoint from that persisted value and sends the real bearer refresh token to it, with no allowlist anywhere on the path.

Root cause on `origin/main` (`e06b42674b4db8af0677d9d88009555768428223`):

`refreshGitHubCopilotToken` in `src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts` builds the endpoint straight from the raw domain:

```ts
// before
const domain = enterpriseDomain || "github.com";
const urls = getUrls(domain); // https://api.${domain}/copilot_internal/v2/token
// ...
Authorization: `Bearer ${refreshToken}`,
```

The provider hook feeds the persisted field in unchecked (`refreshToken` -> `refreshGitHubCopilotToken(creds.refresh, creds.enterpriseUrl)`), and `getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl` has the same gap on its enterprise fallback (that URL carries the access token). The repo already ships a hardened, fail-closed allowlist for exactly this, `normalizeGithubCopilotDomain` (public `github.com` plus `*.ghe.com` tenants only), but the legacy oauth refresh path never calls it.

This is the audited legacy oauth+enterpriseUrl shape only; the shipped provider plugin stores `type: 'token'` credentials and keeps the domain in the allowlisted `githubDomain` config, so it is unaffected. Reachable for upgrade/legacy-state users via a migrated legacy `auth-profiles.json` or direct tampering of the on-disk store.

## Why This Change Was Made

A persisted credential origin is different from a config value: a config typo should fail closed to the public host, but a stored credential whose origin is not on the allowlist is untrustworthy, so the token should not be sent anywhere derived from it. This change rejects the unsupported origin at the refresh boundary and points the user at reauthentication, rather than silently guessing the origin is `github.com`.

- The allowlist plus a new `isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain` predicate move to a dependency-free leaf `src/plugin-sdk/github-copilot-domain.ts`, re-exported from `provider-auth.ts` so the public SDK surface is unchanged. The leaf exists because `github-copilot.ts` cannot import `provider-auth.ts` (that would close a module cycle `github-copilot -> provider-auth -> auth-profiles/oauth -> llm/oauth registry -> github-copilot`).
- `refreshGitHubCopilotToken` now throws for a present-but-unsupported `enterpriseDomain` before constructing any URL or issuing any request, so no bearer token leaves the process for an unsupported origin.
- `getUrls` and `getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl` still coerce through the allowlist (config/device/login and the model base-url fallback keep the shipped fail-closed-to-public behavior; the individual-account default is preserved). `modifyModels` routes through that chokepoint.
- `formatAuthDoctorHint` gains a `github-copilot` short-circuit (mirroring the existing `qwen-portal` reauth hint) that guides the user to re-authenticate when a stored copilot oauth profile has an unsupported enterprise domain. It surfaces both on auth-resolution failure and in `openclaw doctor`.

This closes the P0 egress by reusing shipped hardening and enforces reauthentication rather than a silent repoint. No doctor migration rewrite of persisted `enterpriseUrl` is added: coercing it to `github.com` on migration would mask the reject and repoint the token to the public host, so the runtime reject plus the reauth hint are the whole path, leaving any deeper upgrade-migration policy to the maintainer. Note this issue carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`, `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`, and `clawsweeper:needs-security-review`.

## User Impact

A user with a legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth profile carrying a non-allowlisted `enterpriseUrl` no longer leaks their bearer refresh token on background refresh: the refresh fails closed with no network request, and `openclaw doctor` / auth resolution tells them to re-authenticate. Legitimate public `github.com` and data-residency `*.ghe.com` users see no behavior change. Fixes #103078.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles.doctor.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts` -> pass, including new cases: refresh rejects an unlisted domain without any request, a `*.ghe.com` tenant still works, and the doctor hint guides reauth for an unsupported copilot origin (all fail on pristine main, pass with the patch).
- `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files -> clean.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` -> clean (confirms the extracted leaf breaks the cycle and types resolve). The `tsconfig.core.test.json` lane shows only pre-existing `ui/` dependency errors present identically with and without this diff; none in touched files.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: the legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth refresh path sent the bearer refresh token to a host reconstructed from an unvalidated persisted enterpriseUrl; an unsupported persisted origin should now produce no bearer-bearing request and a reauthentication path
Real environment tested: real production functions driven directly on pristine origin/main e06b42674b4db8af0677d9d88009555768428223 and on the patched tree with identical inputs: refreshGitHubCopilotToken and githubCopilotOAuthProvider.refreshToken (src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts) and formatAuthDoctorHint (src/agents/auth-profiles/doctor.ts); only the outbound fetch() network call was replaced with a stub that records each request URL, all domain-resolution and hint logic ran unmodified
Exact steps or command run after this patch: called refreshGitHubCopilotToken("ghr_real_refresh_token", "attacker.example") and githubCopilotOAuthProvider.refreshToken with a persisted-shaped credential carrying enterpriseUrl "attacker.example", counted the outbound requests, then called refreshGitHubCopilotToken with a supported "acme.ghe.com" domain, and finally requested the doctor hint for a stored copilot oauth profile whose enterpriseUrl is "attacker.example"
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main e06b42674b) -- inputs above
outbound requests for enterpriseUrl "attacker.example" : 2   (https://api.attacker.example/copilot_internal/v2/token, bearer sent)
refreshGitHubCopilotToken / provider.refreshToken error : (none - request was made)
doctor hint for the unsupported-domain profile          : (empty)
outbound request for "acme.ghe.com"                     : https://api.acme.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
outbound requests for enterpriseUrl "attacker.example" : 0
refreshGitHubCopilotToken / provider.refreshToken error : Refusing to refresh GitHub Copilot token for unsupported enterprise domain "attacker.example". Re-authenticate with a supported host (github.com or a *.ghe.com tenant).
doctor hint for the unsupported-domain profile          : This GitHub Copilot OAuth profile has an unsupported enterprise domain and can no longer refresh. Re-authenticate with a supported host (github.com or a *.ghe.com tenant): openclaw onboard --auth-choice github-copilot.
outbound request for "acme.ghe.com"                     : https://api.acme.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token
```
Observed result after fix: an unsupported persisted enterprise domain now produces zero outbound requests (the bearer token is never sent) and both refresh entry points reject with a reauthentication message, while the doctor hint guides reauthentication; a supported *.ghe.com tenant still reaches its own host unchanged
What was not tested: no live GitHub Copilot account or real device-code login was exercised; the outbound fetch() was stubbed since sending live bearer credentials to a real third-party host is out of scope for a safe repro; the interactive loginGitHubCopilot flow has no current caller and was not driven end to end

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Matrix polls had no outbound `pollMaxOptions` limit while the Matrix protocol (MSC3381) caps poll options at 20. Other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12) all declare their protocol limits.
- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and pass `maxOptions: 20` explicitly in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior.
- What changed:
  - `extensions/matrix/src/outbound.ts` — added `pollMaxOptions: 20` to `matrixOutbound`
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.ts` — `buildPollStartContent` passes `maxOptions: 20` explicitly
  - `src/polls.ts` — restored public helper contract (no global default)
- What did NOT change: `normalizePollInput` omitted-limit semantics; other channel implementations.

## ClawSweeper review fixes

**P1: Keep the generic poll limit caller-configured** — Restored `normalizePollInput` public contract: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit (preserving existing behavior for all callers). The 20-option Matrix protocol limit now lives in Matrix-owned code: `matrixOutbound.pollMaxOptions = 20` and `buildPollStartContent(..., { maxOptions: 20 })`. Channels that already declare their limits (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, etc.) are unaffected. Third-party and generic gateway callers that omit `maxOptions` retain their existing behavior.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Matrix polls were missing the 20-option protocol limit. Now enforced at the Matrix boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** Vitest unit tests for Matrix poll types and outbound adapter.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm test src/polls.test.ts
  pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts
  pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/outbound.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # Matrix poll-types boundary tests
  buildPollStartContent with 20 options → answers.length = 20  ✓
  buildPollStartContent with 21 options → throws "at most 20"  ✓

  # Matrix outbound declares protocol limit
  matrixOutbound.pollMaxOptions = 20  ✓

  # Public helper contract preserved
  normalizePollInput with 21 options, no maxOptions → options.length = 21  ✓
  normalizePollInput with 21 options, maxOptions: 20 → throws "at most 20"  ✓
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Matrix 20-option protocol limit enforced at Matrix boundary. Public helper contract preserved.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test files: `src/polls.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/outbound.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Matrix: 20 options accepted, 21 rejected (protocol boundary)
  - Matrix outbound: `pollMaxOptions = 20` declared
  - Public helper: omitted `maxOptions` does not limit (contract preserved)

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Matrix outbound adapter did not declare `pollMaxOptions`, unlike all other poll channel adapters (Discord, WhatsApp, MS Teams, Telegram).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No Matrix-owned poll option limit enforcement.

target.title: perf(agents): avoid intermediate array allocation in subagent registry queries

## What Problem This Solves

Both `listRunsForRequesterFromRuns` and `listRunsForControllerFromRuns` spread the full `Map.values()` into an intermediate array before filtering. For registries with thousands of records, this allocates a full-size intermediate array that is immediately discarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `[...runs.values()].filter(...)` pattern creates two allocations: the spread array holding all records, then the filtered result. Replacing with a direct `for...of` loop + conditional `push()` eliminates the intermediate array entirely.

This is a **narrow in-memory allocation cleanup** on the existing full-snapshot scan path. It does **not** implement scoped/indexed SQLite reads from #105423.

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown; 1 MiB is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IDENTITY_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` covering normal load and an oversized file that exceeds the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
  # 9 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a workspace with an oversized `IDENTITY.md` (2 MiB) and ran `loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace`. The loader returns `null` instead of buffering the oversized file:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (9 tests) 119ms
     ✓ loads identity values from IDENTITY.md
     ✓ returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.05s
```

The oversized identity file is rejected with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`, and the agent loader falls back to no custom identity rather than risking OOM.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

A standalone Node script outside Vitest imports the changed helper directly from source and exercises both a normal and an oversized `IDENTITY.md`:

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-101447.mjs

=== Normal IDENTITY.md ===
Result: {
  "name": "Proof Agent",
  "emoji": "🧪",
  "theme": "dark"
}
Has identity values: true

=== Oversized IDENTITY.md (2 MiB) ===
loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace result: null
Treated as missing (returns null): true

=== Underlying bounded reader behavior ===
readRegularFileSync threw: File exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp/IDENTITY.md

=== Cleanup ===
Removed temp workspace: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp

Standalone proof complete.
```

The proof script is `/tmp/proof-101447.mjs` and is not committed to the repo.

target.title: perf(tasks): reduce peak memory in snapshotTaskRecords by using Array.from with mapper
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`listTaskRecordsUnsorted` cloned ALL task records upfront via `snapshotTaskRecords`, then callers filtered in a second pass. For large task archives (thousands of records) where only a few match the status/agent/session filter, the entire database was cloned before any filtering could discard records.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before: `clone ALL (O(N)) → filter → sort → slice`  
After:  `iterate Map → filter during iteration → clone only matching (O(M)) → sort → slice`

The optional `filter` predicate on `listTaskRecordsUnsorted` lets callers apply their filter during the single Map iteration, so only records that survive the filter are cloned. When no filter is provided, behavior is identical to the original full snapshot.

## User Impact

- Eliminates O(N) pre-clone when the caller filters by status/agent/session
- Peak memory drops from O(N) to O(M) where M = matched records ≪ N for typical queries
- No behavioral change — output is identical
- Backward-compatible API (optional parameter)

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `6d407c3cff874e419e667e60480cefc1a834a6e6` (rebased onto current `main` `e261fa60`; single clean commit; no production clone counters)

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## Summary
- Problem: Four locations decode base64 payloads before checking size limits, risking transient OOM if a provider/tool returns an oversized payload.
- Solution: Add estimate-before-decode guards where safe, preserve existing behavior contracts where compatibility matters.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`: writeCliImages adds maxBytes param, estimates before Buffer.from
  - `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts`: Estimates decoded size before canonicalization to avoid transient string allocation
  - `src/agents/utils/image-resize.ts`: Removed pre-decode check to preserve resize capability for legitimate larger images
  - `src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts`: Restored original return type to maintain plugin SDK compatibility
- What did NOT change: resizeImage still attempts resize before rejecting; generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 still returns guaranteed result.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Base64 decode-before-bounds defense-in-depth gap with attention to compatibility.
- **Real environment tested:** Task worktree with node --import tsx direct function invocation.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { resizeImage } from "./src/agents/utils/image-resize.ts"; import { generatedImageAssetFromBase64 } from "./src/image-generation/image-assets.ts"; import { generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 } from "./src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts"; // ... tests ...'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  === Test 1: image-resize preserves resize capability ===
  Medium payload base64 chars: 14000
  Estimated decoded bytes: 10500
  resizeImage result for medium payload: null
  (null expected because Rastermill unavailable in test, but it tried to process)
  
  === Test 2: image-assets estimates before canonicalization ===
  Oversized payload base64 chars: 200
  Estimated decoded bytes: 150
  generatedImageAssetFromBase64 oversized result: undefined
  (undefined expected, rejected before canonicalization)
  generatedImageAssetFromBase64 normal result buffer: tiny-image
  
  === Test 3: music helper preserves SDK contract ===
  generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 return type: object
  generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 fileName: track-1.mp3
  generatedMusicAssetFromBase64 mimeType: audio/mpeg
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:**
  1. image-resize attempts processing for resizeable images instead of early rejection
  2. image-assets rejects oversized payloads before canonicalization (no transient string allocation)
  3. music helper maintains guaranteed return type for SDK compatibility
- **What was not tested:** Live Rastermill resize (requires image processor backend); only verified logic path preserves resize opportunity.

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts, src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts, src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: Oversized base64 payload rejected before canonicalization; normal payloads decode successfully; music helper returns guaranteed result.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Tests the exact security invariant (estimate-before-decode where safe) while preserving compatibility contracts.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: Functions skipped the "estimate decoded bytes before decode" guard in some paths, and applied it incorrectly in others (blocking resize, breaking SDK contracts).
- Missing detection / guardrail: Pre-canonicalization size check in image-assets; understanding that maxBytes is an output target not an input ceiling for resizeImage; SDK compatibility requirement for music helper.

target.title: fix(ai): clean up abort listener after provider retry sleep
target.body:
Closes #105422

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived OpenAI/ChatGPT provider retry waits would leave an `abort` listener registered on the shared request signal after each successful sleep, accumulating closures and timer handles over many retries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry `sleep` helper registered an anonymous abort listener and only cleared the timeout on abort. On the normal timeout-completion path it resolved without removing the listener. The helper now uses a named abort callback with single-settlement protection and removes the listener on both successful completion and abort, matching other transport cleanup patterns. Focused regression tests lock the lifecycle in.

Open linked PR #105478 only added `{ once: true }`, which does not remove the listener after a successful wait when the signal is never aborted. This PR implements the ClawSweeper-guided symmetric cleanup and adds tests.

## User Impact

Operators and sessions that retry ChatGPT/OpenAI-compatible requests no longer accumulate orphaned abort listeners on long-lived abort signals. Retry timing and abort rejection behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts -t "sleepForTest abort listener lifecycle"
# 4 passed | 32 skipped

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts
# 36 passed

pnpm test:changed
# packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts — 36 passed

pnpm check:changed
# ok: conflict markers, changelog attributions, wildcard re-exports, duplicates, dependency pins, format changed files
# failed: Plugin SDK API baseline — same hash mismatch reproduces on clean origin/main without this change (unrelated host/checkout drift; not introduced by sleep lifecycle edit)

git diff --check  # clean
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: After a successful retry sleep, the abort listener registered on the caller's signal is removed so repeated waits on one non-aborted signal do not accumulate listeners/closures.
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at branch `fix/105422-abort-listener-sleep`, Node 24, focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: On `origin/main`, `sleep` does `setTimeout(resolve, ms)` and `addEventListener("abort", …)` with no `removeEventListener` on the resolve path, so each completed wait leaves a listener on a long-lived signal.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts -t "sleepForTest abort listener lifecycle"`
  2. Spy-based cases call `sleepForTest` three times on one `AbortController` signal and assert each `addEventListener("abort", fn)` is matched by `removeEventListener("abort", fn)`.
  3. Abort-during-wait and already-aborted paths still reject with `Request was aborted` and clean up.
- Evidence after fix: 4/4 lifecycle tests passed; full provider file 36/36 passed; `pnpm test:changed` green for the touched surface.
- Control check: Assertions target the same listener function reference added and removed; sibling transport tests in the same file still pass (no change to retry delay policy or error mapping).
- Observed result after fix: Successful sleeps unregister their abort listener; multiple waits no longer leave N listeners; abort still rejects promptly.
- What was not tested: Live paid OpenAI/ChatGPT cloud turns; heap profiling under production load; linked PR #105478 merge conflict resolution (this branch is independent and complete).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human/operator oversight is via the normal OpenClaw contributor PR review process.

target.title: [codex] Link heartbeat commitment questions to replies
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the architectural gap where inferred commitment heartbeats can ask open-ended questions from a proactive heartbeat session, while the user's later answer lands in the target conversation without durable context tying it back to that question.

It now covers both failure modes from the reports:

- Delivered heartbeat questions are mirrored into durable pending-question context on the target session, then drained into the next user-triggered prompt exactly once.
- Inferred commitments get a resolution pass before persistence/delivery, so later same-session completion evidence, including tool-verified completion, can dismiss stale pending follow-ups instead of sending them.

## Root Cause

Heartbeat commitment delivery can happen in an isolated heartbeat run. The visible proactive question is transcript-only delivery state, and replay intentionally filters `openclaw/delivery-mirror` assistant messages before model calls. That means a later user response can be replayed without the assistant question that prompted it unless the transport provides reply metadata.

A second gap existed upstream: extraction could infer an open-loop follow-up before later turns completed and verified the work, but there was no pre-delivery resolution pass against existing pending commitments.

## Approach

- Add `SessionHeartbeatPendingQuestion` / `heartbeatPendingQuestions` to session state.
- Queue a pending question only after a due commitment heartbeat is actually sent successfully.
- Drain pending heartbeat questions only for `trigger: "user"` prompt builds.
- Cache the drained pending-question context alongside plugin next-turn injections for retry stability.
- Teach the extractor to emit top-level `resolved` entries for existing pending commitments closed by the latest exchange.
- Validate resolutions against the current item's `existingPending` dedupe keys and confidence threshold.
- Dismiss matching active commitments before upserting new candidates, and skip creating a candidate resolved in the same extraction item.
- Reserve the new session-entry key so plugin slot projection cannot claim it.

## ClawSweeper / Review Notes

This is intentionally architectural, not wording-only. It avoids depending on Telegram reply context, gives the next ordinary user turn a durable resolution path, and prevents stale inferred commitments from reaching heartbeat delivery when later verified completion has already closed the loop.

The PR branch was fast-forwarded with the resolution-pass commit on top of the existing pending-question fix.

Current PR head: `b329e57e77fbed0b103cefe726a973797dd8d6cc`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Durable pending-question linkage for proactive commitment questions. A delivered heartbeat question is persisted on the target session with source metadata, then drained into the next user-turn prompt context exactly once.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout `/Users/jeeves/openclaw`, branch `codex/commitment-pending-question-context`, head `b329e57e77`, Node v26.0.0 with `tsx`, disposable temp session store under `/tmp/openclaw-pending-question-proof-REDACTED/sessions.json`. No Telegram/network send and no live user session data were used for this proof.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Set `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-proof-missing-config.json` to avoid reading the live installed config.
2. Seeded a disposable `sessions.json` entry for `agent:main:telegram:user-155462274`.
3. Imported the real source functions from `src/config/sessions/pending-question-context.ts` via `node --import tsx`.
4. Called `enqueueHeartbeatPendingQuestion(...)` with redacted May 9-style commitment/source metadata.
5. Read the session store to verify the queued question and source message id were persisted.
6. Called `drainHeartbeatPendingQuestionContext(...)` for the same session and read the store again.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "enqueued": true,
  "queuedText": "Want me to check your Mega Millions ticket from last night?",
  "queuedCommitmentIds": ["cm_demo"],
  "queuedSourceMessageIds": ["14517"],
  "contextIncludesQuestion": true,
  "contextMentionsInternalSuppression": true,
  "queueAfterDrain": null,
  "tempSessionStore": "/tmp/openclaw-pending-question-proof-REDACTED/sessions.json"
}
```

Observed result after fix: The enqueue path returned `true`, the pending question persisted with the source message id, the drained context included the original proactive question plus the instruction to hide internal heartbeat/commitment machinery, and the subsequent store read showed `queueAfterDrain: null`, proving one-shot drainage for the next user turn.

What was not tested: This proof did not send a real Telegram message or inspect a real lottery ticket image. Physical transport delivery remains covered by the existing heartbeat outbound path; this PR targets the missing durable reply-linkage layer after successful delivery.

Behavior or issue addressed: Inferred commitments are resolved before delivery when later same-session evidence shows the loop is already complete, matching the Gmail reauth false-positive pattern.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout `/Users/jeeves/openclaw`, branch `codex/commitment-pending-question-context`, head `b329e57e77`, Node v26.0.0 with `tsx`, disposable commitment store under `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)`. No live installed commitment store and no Gmail account credentials were read.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Set `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` to a disposable temp directory.
2. Seeded the real commitment store API with a pending inferred Gmail reauth follow-up using id `cm_mp4j2jsy_9a9a2f424e` and dedupe key `gmail-reauth:sprichert@gmail.com`.
3. Imported `persistCommitmentExtractionResult(...)` from `src/commitments/extraction.ts` via `node --import tsx`.
4. Persisted an extraction result whose latest assistant turn reported tool-verified Gmail reauth completion and emitted both a repeated candidate and a high-confidence `resolved` entry for the same dedupe key.
5. Reloaded the commitment store through the real store API.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "proof": "resolved pending inferred Gmail reauth commitment before delivery",
  "createdCount": 0,
  "finalCommitments": [
    {
      "id": "cm_mp4j2jsy_9a9a2f424e",
      "dedupeKey": "gmail-reauth:sprichert@gmail.com",
      "status": "dismissed",
      "dismissedAtMs": 1778752800000,
      "suggestedText": "Did the gog Gmail reauth go through for sprichert@gmail.com?"
    }
  ]
}
```

Observed result after fix: The pending inferred follow-up was dismissed before delivery, and `createdCount: 0` proves the repeated same-key candidate was not recreated in the same extraction pass.

What was not tested: This proof did not run a live Gmail OAuth flow. It exercises the OpenClaw commitment extraction/persistence path that decides whether an already-completed inferred follow-up remains eligible for heartbeat delivery.

## Validation

- `CI=true pnpm test src/commitments/extraction.test.ts src/commitments/runtime.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.commitments.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.prompt-helpers.test.ts`

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. The registry carries a persisted readiness contract: `readiness ('provisioning'|'ready')` (closed union; additive `ensureColumn` migration per repo precedent — backfill-as-ready is provably safe because no release tag contains the worktrees feature, and unreleased-main builds inserted rows only post-provisioning). The claim inserts `provisioning`; a single UPDATE flips to `ready` only after copy+setup succeed. Every usable-record path is gated on ready (`findLiveByOwner` filters in SQL; the entry shortcut and claim-loser throw a closed `WorktreeProvisioningError`; `restore()` revives as ready; provisioning rows are leases with heartbeats (`lastActiveAt` bumped at claim, post-copy, and at the ready flip): gc reaps only leases SILENT past `PROVISIONING_STALE_MS` — a persisted holder-liveness signal, so claim age alone can never kill a live-but-slow holder — restoring background recovery for auto-named orphans, while a reaped-mid-flight create fails closed with `WorktreeProvisioningReapedError`; a provisioning row whose directory vanished is hard-deleted (branch + row; no snapshot, no user work) so the name stays genuinely retriable). The gateway protocol's `WorktreeRecordSchema` gains an additive optional `readiness` enum (no version bump). Normal (non-adopting) `create()` uses the identical claim-early ordering (claim immediately after `git worktree add`; both paths share one claim → provision-as-holder → holder-only-cleanup helper), establishing the invariant that an in-flight create always holds a live row — so the no-row+live-worktree signature genuinely means a crashed create, and an in-flight worktree can never be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name call. Every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced through the one claim. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc keeps upstream's preserve-only behavior for foreign/detached and live git-listed worktrees (only dead debris and stale provisioning rows are cleaned); no protocol version bump; no changes to snapshot semantics; web UI status label deliberately unchanged (would pull in i18n regeneration disproportionate to this PR).

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #103239
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no adopt-or-repair path for the crashed-create signature; `create()`'s branch-exists guard had no way to distinguish "user's foreign branch" from "our own crashed create()".
- Contributing context (if known): the registry has no `name` column (name derives from the path's last segment), so adoption needs no extra bookkeeping — the orphan is fully re-derivable from path + branch.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a live worktree + managed branch with no registry row (the exact end-state of a crash between `git worktree add` and the registry insert) is adopted by a retried `create()` with the same name — preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId`, re-running provisioning (include files + setup script restored, real `baseRef` recorded), and holding the loser-touches-nothing / holder-only-destruction invariants under deterministic interleavings; gc during an in-flight normal `create()` adopts nothing and exactly one live row remains; a parked in-flight create cannot be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name retry (same-owner and foreign-owner both covered, setup executes exactly once); a failing setup leaves no worktree, branch, or registry row.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests use the real `git` binary and real SQLite registry (the file's established pattern — no mocks), produce the crash end-state via production code (`create()` then deleting only the registry row), and assert through the public service API only.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): "deletes unregistered orphan debris but preserves git-listed worktrees" covers the foreign/detached case and stays green, locking in that non-managed worktrees are never claimed.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — two new tests added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- A retried `create()` with the same name after a crashed create now succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record) instead of failing with `branch already exists`.
- gc behavior is unchanged from upstream (preserve-only for live worktrees); foreign or detached-HEAD worktrees are unaffected.
- Concurrent same-path registrations can no longer produce duplicate live registry rows (atomic claim; loser gets the existing "name already in use" semantics).
- `list()` now shows a worktree from claim-time (during provisioning) rather than after setup completes; failed creates still end with no registry row.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): "branch already exists" (dead end; manual git surgery required)

After:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): exact orphan signature -> atomic path claim -> re-provision
     (owner + real base preserved) -> returns record
  -> claim loser (concurrent registration won): touches nothing; standard in-use semantics
  -> gc: preserve-only (unchanged upstream behavior)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A. Adoption is gated on an exact `git worktree list --porcelain` path + `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>` branch match; fabricating that state requires local filesystem/git access equivalent to what `create()` already requires. `insertRegistryWorktree` is the same call path `create()` already uses.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26 (arm64); fix is platform-independent (pure git + SQLite service logic)
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / bun, source checkout
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): default `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`-backed state

### Steps

1. `ManagedWorktreeService.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` and kill the process after `git worktree add` completes but before the registry insert (repro: create normally, then delete only the registry row — identical end state).
2. Run `service.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` again.

### Expected

- retried create succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record); gc preserves the orphan untouched.

### Actual

- Before this PR: gc skips it forever; retried create throws `branch already exists: openclaw/task-1`. After this PR: expected behavior (see tests).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Before (tests added, fix stashed):

```
❯ |agents| src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts (24 tests | 2 failed)
FAIL … adopts a worktree orphaned when create() crashed …, during gc()
  AssertionError: expected undefined to match object {…}
FAIL … adopts an orphaned worktree instead of throwing on a retried create() …
  Error: branch already exists: openclaw/orphan-retry
```

After:

```
pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  41 passed (41) agents shard + 23 passed state shard
```

Real-behavior proof on the FROZEN FINAL head e5b7677497 (all four requested scenarios — active holder survives gc, SIGKILLed holder reaped after lease expiry and recreated fully provisioned, missing-path claim cleaned to a retriable name, pre-column DB backfills ready): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4947439791. Earlier ordering-specific transcript: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4944938951 — Window B is a genuine mid-provisioning SIGKILL (exit 137) showing the crash state is observable (claim-time row, missing setup marker), gc preserves it, and the operator recovery path works end-to-end (remove() cleans worktree+branch, fresh create fully provisions); Window A (add→claim, no user code) is a labeled constructed end-state recovered by retried-create adoption with full re-provisioning. Supersedes the earlier transcript (#issuecomment-4937129438), which demonstrated the pre-claim-early ordering.

Also green on the touched surface: `pnpm tsgo:core` (exit 0), `oxlint` (0 findings), `oxfmt --check` (formatted). Note: repo-wide `pnpm check` currently fails in its preflight `npm shrinkwrap guard` on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout in this environment (`ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` for the `defu` override) — pre-existing and unrelated; no lockfile/override files are touched by this PR.

The previously-acknowledged gc-vs-create double-insert race is now eliminated by the atomic path claim (deterministic interleaving tests cover both directions, with a pasted negative control showing the pre-claim code produces the duplicate row). Remaining narrow edge deliberately out of scope: a lingering *removed* registry row at the same path still blocks create()-side adoption for a fresh orphan (name-reuse-after-remove + crash sequence).

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: full scoped test suite (25/25) against real git + real SQLite locally, including both new adoption tests and the pre-existing foreign-worktree preservation test; typecheck/lint/format on the touched files.
- Edge cases checked: detached-HEAD foreign worktree (preserved), bare branch collision without a live worktree (still throws), owner preservation (`workboard`/`ownerId`) on retried-create adoption including `findLiveByOwner()` lookup, crash-before-setup retry re-provisioning (include file + setup marker restored, real base recorded), and full cleanup on a failing setup script during adoption-retry.
- What you did **not** verify: a literal `kill -9` mid-`create()` on a production gateway (the crash end-state is reproduced through the service's own code paths instead); the two out-of-scope narrow edges above.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: schema/migration surface (new `readiness` column).
  - Mitigation: additive `ensureColumn` per the repo's established migration pattern; backfill default provably correct (see body); legacy-DB backfill test included; fresh-vs-migrated CHECK divergence is unobservable to prod writes (closed TS union at every write site).
- Risk: adopting a worktree that a user intentionally created outside the managed API at the exact managed path on an `openclaw/<name>` branch.
  - Mitigation: that state is indistinguishable from (and equivalent to) a crashed managed create; adoption only registers it — it never deletes or modifies the worktree.
- Risk: concurrent adoption attempts (gc vs retried create) racing for one path.
  - Mitigation: eliminated — adoption is a single-statement atomic path claim with explicit loser handling; losers never provision, mutate, or destroy; covered by deterministic interleaving tests in both directions.

## Summary

- Problem: one-shot cron jobs that completed successfully could remain visible as `running` with null completion fields while later jobs from the same due batch were still executing or stuck.
- Why it matters: operators and integrations saw completed cron-triggered sessions as still active, and those stale `runningAtMs` entries could suppress logical re-enqueue/dedupe decisions.
- What changed: cron timer workers now persist each completed due-job outcome immediately under the cron store lock instead of buffering outcomes until the whole due-job batch drains.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not change cron scheduling semantics, job selection, delivery behavior, task classification, or retry policy.

```text
After:
```

target.title: perf(tasks): reduce peak memory in snapshotTaskRecords by using Array.from with mapper
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`listTaskRecordsUnsorted` cloned ALL task records upfront via `snapshotTaskRecords`, then callers filtered in a second pass. For large task archives (thousands of records) where only a few match the status/agent/session filter, the entire database was cloned before any filtering could discard records.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before: `clone ALL (O(N)) → filter → sort → slice`  
After:  `iterate Map → filter during iteration → clone only matching (O(M)) → sort → slice`

The optional `filter` predicate on `listTaskRecordsUnsorted` lets callers apply their filter during the single Map iteration, so only records that survive the filter are cloned. When no filter is provided, behavior is identical to the original full snapshot.

## User Impact

- Eliminates O(N) pre-clone when the caller filters by status/agent/session
- Peak memory drops from O(N) to O(M) where M = matched records ≪ N for typical queries
- No behavioral change — output is identical
- Backward-compatible API (optional parameter)

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.

  - `git diff --check` - passed.

target.title: perf(agents): avoid intermediate array allocation in subagent registry queries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Both `listRunsForRequesterFromRuns` and `listRunsForControllerFromRuns` spread the full `Map.values()` into an intermediate array before filtering. For registries with thousands of records, this allocates a full-size intermediate array that is immediately discarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `[...runs.values()].filter(...)` pattern creates two allocations: the spread array holding all records, then the filtered result. Replacing with a direct `for...of` loop + conditional `push()` eliminates the intermediate array entirely.

This is a **narrow in-memory allocation cleanup** on the existing full-snapshot scan path. It does **not** implement scoped/indexed SQLite reads from #105423.

## User Impact

- Fewer peak allocations when listing requester/controller runs against a large in-memory registry snapshot
- Same matched results and ordering semantics
- Does not change persistence load scope (full snapshot + linear scan remain)

### Static / unit gates


```typescript
// Before — Allocates full intermediate array before filter
[...runs.values()].filter((entry) => entry.requesterSessionKey === key);
```

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock-mantle): dedupe the IAM token-failure diagnostic per region (#67288)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #67288. On hosts with no usable AWS credentials (Raspberry Pi installs, default Docker images), the `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin attempts IAM bearer-token generation on every implicit-discovery call (every catalog refresh) and logs `[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` **every time** it fails. The user-visible symptom is continuous log noise on installs that never configured AWS.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix dedupes the failure diagnostic per region for the process lifetime instead of gating the IAM chain itself:

- `generateBearerTokenFromIam` keeps running the AWS default credential chain on every call — hosts that rely on late-arriving credentials (instance roles, IRSA, SSO) still start working the moment the chain succeeds, with no opt-in config.
- The `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` debug line is emitted **at most once per region per process** (`iamTokenFailureLogged` set). A successful token generation for that region clears the marker, so a later regression logs again.

An earlier revision of this PR short-circuited discovery entirely when no AWS env creds were present; that approach was **abandoned after review** because it broke instance-role/IRSA/SSO hosts whose credentials are not visible in env vars. The current diff contains no credential gate and adds no config surface.

**Operator-observability tradeoff (explicit):** for a region that keeps failing, only the *first* failure's details are logged per process. If the underlying failure reason later changes (e.g. from "no credentials" to a network error) while generation keeps failing, the new details are not logged until a token generation succeeds for that region or the gateway process restarts. This trades per-request detail freshness for eliminating unbounded per-request log spam.

## User Impact

- Installs without AWS credentials see the diagnostic once per region instead of on every request.
- Hosts with working or late-arriving IAM chains are unaffected: token generation is still attempted every call.
- No config changes, no new keys, no behavior change for `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` users or explicit `discovery.enabled: false`.

## Evidence

Exact-head (c0e8c4d134b) regression run:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts

 ✓ logs 'IAM token generation unavailable' at most once per region across repeated implicit-discovery calls (#67288)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

The regression drives the production `resolveImplicitMantleProvider` three times with a failing token provider and asserts, via a captured discovery-subsystem logger, that:
- the token provider factory ran on **all 3** calls (IAM-chain fallback semantics preserved — no short-circuit), and
- the `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` diagnostic was emitted **exactly once**, with the expected `region` metadata — removing the dedupe guard fails the test.

Not yet supplied: redacted current-head runtime logs from a real credential-less host showing the single diagnostic across repeated catalog refreshes (the remaining reviewer ask).

Part of #67288.

target.title: fix(ui): isolate retained test modules
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The non-isolated Control UI test runner resets modules while jsdom retains its custom-element registry and Vitest can retain imported production modules. The terminal, native-link, and approval-page tests used fixed test tags, so later evaluations could mount constructors from an earlier graph. The terminal component could also keep the earlier graph's runtime mock, making six terminal tests fail while the current mock saw no calls. The approval page could similarly format with an earlier graph's English locale after the current test selected German.

The config-search tests also reached private helpers through `config-form.node.ts`, leaving test-only re-exports and types in that production module. #105705 removed those exports, but its `checks-ui` failure and this PR's dependency failure created a circular landing block.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Give each terminal/native-link test-module evaluation a fresh UUID-suffixed custom-element tag.
- Give the approval page and its context provider matching fresh tags so locale, context, and the mounted element share one module graph.
- Keep one typed terminal-runtime mock identity on the worker global so retained production imports and the current test graph call the same mock.
- Import config-search helpers from their owning module and remove the private forwarding exports/types. The exact contributor commit from #105705 is retained with Vincent Koc as author.

This completes the isolation intent of #103345 and keeps each test bound to its current module graph without changing product code paths.
